question: Can a tiny, separate regulator — its own key, its own state, its own baseline — visit every node of a mesh in turn, check each against that node's OWN rules and baseline (drift, rate, budget, health), catch an injected drift within a few visits and damp it, while it can only observe, throttle, pause and report, cannot build, publish, spend or change code, runs on Pi-class compute, and leaves every node running (and Simon alerted) when it dies or drifts?
why: Simon's spec, 2026-10-28, UPGRADE 3 (the independent regulator), built first because it makes the other two safer to run. Inspired by Gary W. Floyd's NexusGrid as he described it in chat (Gary W. Floyd, Lumiea Systems Research Division — ThunderStruck Service LLC); designed from that description only — no parity with his system is claimed, and the comparison with his real implementation follows his catch-up call. The field and damping are the GEP-BES forms from Gary W. Floyd, Lumiea Systems Research Division — ThunderStruck Service LLC — "GEP-Based Security: Behavioral Entropy Signatures for Cybersecurity and DevOps," 2025 (CC BY 4.0), §3.
honesty: The regulator cannot operate: its only verbs are observe, throttle, pause, report and resume (a low-stakes node only).

The BES layer (a sibling build) had not landed when this was sealed: its kernels were uncommitted. The regulator's drift and envelope checks are this build's own, behind an interface with BES's shape (parts → field → verdict; envelope stages), so BES's kernels can slot in when they land.
No Raspberry Pi is available here. R3 is measured on this laptop (12th Gen Intel Core i7-1255U) and scaled by a deliberately pessimistic proxy factor; it is a proxy, said as one.

data.what: The REAL public commit histories of ten estate builds at pinned commits (tools/nodes.mjs, re-derived from GitHub in CI). Each build is a node; each commit one action { t: committer time, area: the part it touched most (src/streams.mjs areaOf), files: files touched }. Nothing else is kept.
data.split: per node, the first 60% of its actions (by time, floor, at least 1) are FIT — the only actions any baseline, band or budget is calibrated on; the rest are HELD-OUT, where every claim is measured.
data.highStakesWhy: the two nodes that speak or act outward for the estate; a pause on them is lifted only by Simon

design.visits: One visit per node per hour; node i (in data order) at hh:00 + 6·i minutes. A visit sees only what the node has done since its previous visit (no overlap) plus its 24-hour attempt count and its journal since the last verified head.
design.parts: Three parts of behaviour, each a symbol per action: area (9 symbols), files bucket (1, 2, 3–4, 5–8, 9–16, 17+), gap bucket (floor(log2(1 + minutes since the node's previous action)), capped at 9; an action with no predecessor has no gap). A part's window entropy is Miller–Madow corrected: H_plugin + (m − 1)/(2n), m = symbols seen.
design.baseline: Per node and part, from its FIT windows (hourly visits over its FIT period that saw ≥ 5 actions): S_b = (q05 + q95)/2 and ε = max(0.25, (q95 − q05)/2). A node with fewer than 8 qualifying FIT windows uses the band pooled over every node's FIT windows. The gaps' coefficient of variation floor cvFloor = min(0.35, q05 of FIT window CVs), pooled the same way; a floor of 0 never fires.
design.drift: Gary's field per part, E_p = σ(8·(|S_w − S_b| − ε)), only when the window holds ≥ 5 actions (N_MIN). The regularity row (Gary's finding that scripted automation fails by being overly regular): window gap CV < cvFloor → E_reg = 1. E_drift = the worst part (BES's 'the worst decides').
design.budget: The node's envelope: perHour = max(6, 2 × its FIT max actions in one clock hour), perDay = max(20, 2 × its FIT max in one UTC day). r = max(attempts since the last visit / perHour, attempts in the last 24 h / perDay); attempts count executed AND held actions. E_budget = 0 if r ≤ 1, else min(1, 0.6 + 0.4·(r − 1)).
design.rate: β|∇S| with β = 1: g = E_t − E_{t−1} when the field rises; g ≥ 0.5 is rapid escalation (reason 'rate').
design.health: Each node keeps a hash-chained journal of what it executed (SHA-256, each record names its predecessor). At each visit the regulator re-verifies from the head it last verified; a rewritten history or a broken link fails health.
design.damping: Pressure P_t = 0.5·P_{t−1} + 0.5·E_t, E_t = max(E_drift, E_budget). While a node is paused its pressure is frozen (no evidence is not evidence of health).
design.ladder: pause if health fails, or P ≥ 0.85, or r > 1 at this visit and the previous one; else throttle if P ≥ 0.6 or r > 1; else watch if P ≥ 0.3 or E_t ≥ 0.5 or g ≥ 0.5; else steady.
design.effects: throttle: the node holds every second attempt; pause: it holds every attempt. Both carry a 3-hour lease renewed by each visit that repeats or strengthens them; a lapsed lease ends them (the node runs on its own gates). A pause on a low-stakes node is lifted by the regulator only on probation (throttle) after a cool-down of 12 h × 2^(k−1) for that node's k-th pause; a high-stakes node's pause is lifted only by Simon's signed resume and does not lapse.
design.record: Every visit is a record { seq, at, node, verdict, reasons, P, E, r, prev } hash-chained and signed Ed25519 by the regulator's own key (demo key from the public phrase 'watch-dream-remember/regulator/demo'; Simon's key from 'watch-dream-remember/simon/demo').
design.envelope: Signed by Simon's key, naming the regulator's key as holder: scope [observe, throttle, pause, report, resume], budget 0 units, at most 2 NEW pauses mesh-wide in any 6 hours, a validity window and a nonce. Checked in stages: shape → issuer → holder → signature → forbidden → scope → high-stakes target → window → expiry → revoked → budget → rate → admitted. Forbidden verbs (build, publish, spend, code-change and their kin) are refused even inside an envelope Simon signed.
design.nodeGuard: A node honours a throttle or pause only if its signature verifies under the pinned regulator key and the envelope admits it (including the pause rate, read from the regulator's public log). A node checks the log every 15 minutes; no visit to it for more than 2 hours raises 'regulator-silent' to Simon; a refused verdict raises 'regulator-drift'.

injections.starts: two per node per type, t0 = heldStart + U·(heldEnd − heldStart), U from the seeded PRNG in order node → type → k
injections.horizon: 24 hours after t0; the node's real actions continue alongside

types.runaway-fast: the node's most common FIT area with its median FIT file count, repeated at an exact period of 3600 s / max(20, 3 × FIT max per clock hour)
types.runaway-quiet: the same identical action every 10 minutes exactly (6 an hour — in budget, normal speed)
types.scatter-quiet: every 5–15 minutes (uniform), a uniformly random area of the 9 and a uniformly random file count 1–20 (a hijack driving at normal speed)
types.overrun: actions resampled from the node's own FIT actions with exponential gaps at max(20, 3 × FIT max per clock hour) an hour (its own mix, too much of it)
types.health: at t0 one earlier journal record is rewritten (its area changed) — the node's history no longer matches what the regulator verified

claims.claim: An injected drift is detected within 3 visits and damped.
claims.pass: (a) for each of runaway-fast, runaway-quiet, scatter-quiet and overrun, at least 19 of its 20 trials draw a verdict ≥ watch with a reason of drift, rate or budget within the first 3 visits to that node after t0; for health, 20 of 20 trials are paused at the first visit after t0; (b) for each of the four behaviour types, injected actions executed ÷ injected actions intended over the 24-hour horizons ≤ 0.25

claims.claim: On the real held-out histories with nothing injected, the regulator pauses nothing and throttles rarely.
claims.pass: 0 pause verdicts across all ten nodes; throttle verdicts ≤ 5% of active visits (visits that saw at least one action)

claims.claim: Every verdict is logged, signed and re-runnable.
claims.pass: every record's signature verifies under the regulator's key, the chain links end to end, and a second run of the same replay ends on the identical chain head

claims.claim: Build, publish, spend and code-change attempts are refused by its envelope, and it holds no means to do them.
claims.pass: every attempt in the battery below is refused at exactly the stage named; the five legitimate verbs are admitted; and its runtime modules (src/regulator.mjs, src/envelope.mjs, src/journal.mjs, src/mesh.mjs) import nothing from node:fs, node:child_process, node:net, node:http, node:https, node:dgram, node:worker_threads, and contain no fetch(, eval(, new Function( or dynamic import(

claims.claim: It runs within a sealed compute bound on a Pi-class device (proxy: this laptop × 50).
claims.pass: over the R1f replay: CPU time per visit p99 ≤ 1 ms and the slowest full round of ten visits ≤ 50 ms on this laptop (so ≤ 2.5 s an hour on a device 50 times slower — under 0.1% of one core); the regulator's whole state ≤ 64 KB as JSON; the same replay under node --jitless (no JIT compiler) keeps p99 per visit ≤ 10 ms

claims.claim: Killing it stops no node and raises an alert; a drifting regulator is contained the same way.
claims.pass: (a) killed at 2026-10-24T12:00:00Z during the real replay: every node's executed actions after the kill + 3 h equal the no-regulator replay exactly, and every node raises 'regulator-silent' at its first 15-minute check more than 2 hours after its last visit; (b) a regulator gone rogue at the same moment (a fresh, validly signed pause for every node at every visit): at most 2 nodes honour a pause, no pause holds longer than one 3-hour lease, every node raises 'regulator-drift' within 1 hour, and every node's executed actions after the rogue start + 3 h equal the no-regulator replay

battery.note: even Simon's signature cannot put a forbidden verb in its scope
any cost at all against a budget of 0
a third new pause in 6 hours

predictions: Written before any regulator code. R1(a) detection: likely for runaway-fast, overrun and health; runaway-quiet rides on the regularity row and scatter-quiet on the area/files bands, which are calibrated on few real windows — either could miss. R1(b) damping: about 0.1 for runaway-fast and overrun, 0.15–0.25 for the quiet types (near the bar). R1f: real build sessions are bursty and focused; budget overruns as builds speed up are the likeliest false throttles; 0 pauses expected but not certain. R2 expected to hold by construction. R3 expected to hold with a wide margin. R4 expected to hold.
